answer: Identity minting requires a unique hardware key seeded by a crystal oscillator's timing jitter, so cloned software identities collide and get rejected. Each new agent must also be grafted onto an existing trust vine: two independent members stake a bond behind it. An attacker wanting N sybils must buy N distinct walnut-sized secure elements and post N bonds, all slashed if any two share a fingerprint. Faking costs more than the rewards it captures.
